description: Neodymium is a chemical element with symbol Nd and atomic number 60, the fourth member of the lanthanide series and one of the rare-earth metals. It is a hard, slightly malleable, silvery metal that quickly tarnishes in air and moisture. When oxidized, neodymium reacts quickly, producing pink, purple/blue, and yellow compounds in various oxidation states.
uses: Neodymium compounds are used as glass dyes and additives, with glasses doped with neodymium used in lasers emitting infrared wavelengths. Neodymium alloys are used to make high-strength permanent magnets widely used in microphones, loudspeakers, headphones, electric motors, and computer hard disk drives. Larger neodymium magnets are used in electric motors with high power-to-weight ratios in hybrid cars and in generators for aircraft and wind turbines.
characteristics: Metallic neodymium has a bright, silvery metallic luster and exists in two allotropic forms with a transformation at about 863°C. It is paramagnetic at room temperature but becomes an antiferromagnet below 20 K, exhibiting complex magnetic phases. Neodymium has a melting point of 1,024°C and boiling point of 3,074°C, usually has oxidation state +3 but can form +2 and +4 states, and corrodes completely in about a year when exposed to ambient conditions.
